newsitem.title: POLAND: MOSTOSTAL-Z HOPES FOR GM CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: MOSTOSTAL-Z HOPES FOR GM CONTRACT.

text.p: The Polish construction company Mostostal Zabrze SA is hoping to win a contract for part of the construction of General Motors' new car factory to be built in the southern town of Gliwice, Mostostal's president said.
Leszek Pietrzak told reporters on Thursday that Mostostal had offered to build the foundation, workshops and car- painting and assembly facilities for GM.
He estimated the value of all construction work at the Gliwice site at about 200 million marks but declined to name the value of the contract for which Mostostal was contending.
"The winner of the tender (for the construction work we are bidding for) will be chosen by the end of the month. We estimate that our chances as very high," Pietrzak said.
He said there were two other tenders for different construction jobs at Gliwice in which Mostostal Zabrze was not participating.
The 470-million-mark automotive plant is expected to assemble 72,000 passenger cars annually from 1998.

The factory, employing 2,000 people in an area threatened by massive lay-offs from the ailing coal-mining industry, will resemble Opel's state-of-the-art assembly plant in the German city of Eisenach.
It will assemble a low-cost family car based on the Opel/Vauxhall Astra model.
The plant will include metal-stamping, welding, paint and final-assembly units, all of which could be expanded after additional investment.
After several years about 60 percent of parts used for assembly would come from Poland.
